evidence.claim: At its eastern end, Sand Bar State Park preserves a large stone bathhouse built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1933–35.
evidence.quote: The most prominent built feature of the park is a large stone bathhouse.  It was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) in 1933–35.

evidence.quote: The upper level of the bathhouse was originally used as living quarters for caretakers and lifeguards but is now used for storage, while the rest of the structure, only modified to provide electricity and plumbing, continues in its original use.

evidence.claim: A stone grill built by the CCC also remains, beside a park whose facilities include a 2,000-foot sand beach.

flags: Formal byway is 184 miles in the council source; catalog map is 74.5 miles. Intro distinguishes the full corridor, but cache does not identify its precise southern endpoint.
Milton appears at mile 2.47 in material despite being the mainland landfall after South Hero in cache. Moments follow the supported north-to-south route rather than that anomalous mileage.
Geology age is repeated by the byway council and secondary cache; no scientific source is saved. Avoided the secondary page’s more sweeping reef superlatives and biological claims.
No current site-manager access notice is cached for Sand Bar or the quarries; no hours or promises of entry are supplied.
